title: Temples ‘of’ Saints: many deny building them to Saints, yet name churches after them as thanks to God and plea to the Patron
source_text: XV. Etenim quamvis Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae negent templa Sanctis esse construenda, in ea tamen consuetudo est ut templa, sive Ecclesiae, ut vocant, hujus aut illius Sancti nomine appellentur, & dicantur, verbi causa, Ecclesia Beatae Virginis, Sancti Petri, Pauli, Francisci, &c. Qua de re mentem suam non omnes ejus Ecclesiae Doctores eodem modo exponunt. Proinde quum aliquod templum, aut aedes sacra dicitur, exempli causa, Sancti Petri, non ideo dicitur, quod sacrificium offeratur Petro, sed quod offeratur Deo in gratiarum actionem pro gloria Sancto Petro data, & simul interpellatur Petrus, tanquam Patronus, & Advocatus apud Deum. De cultu Sanctorum Libro III. cap. 4.
pass_a_gloss: For although the Doctors of the Roman Church deny that temples are to be built to the Saints, yet in that Church the custom is that temples, or Churches as they call them, are named by the name of this or that Saint, and are called, for example, the Church of the Blessed Virgin, of Saint Peter, Paul, Francis, etc. On which matter not all Doctors of that Church explain their mind in the same way. Accordingly when some temple, or sacred house, is called, for example, of Saint Peter, it is not therefore so called because sacrifice is offered to Peter, but because it is offered to God in thanksgiving for the glory given to Saint Peter, and at the same time Peter is appealed to as Patron and Advocate before God. On the Cult of the Saints, Book III, chapter 4.
pass_b_english: Doctors deny temples built to Saints—yet churches everywhere bear Saints’ names.
Explanations diverge; one line: sacrifice still goes to God in thanks for the Saint’s glory, while the Patron is appealed as advocate.

lemmas.gloss: temples are to be built to the Saints
